news.title: Infantino given two-week deadline to come clean over World Cup sell-off
news.lede: European football chiefs make fresh demands for transparency as they remain unsatisfied by Fifa president’s apologies. Gianni Infantino has been told he has two weeks to answer 42 outstanding questions on his various controversies by European football leaders who attended last week’s Fifa Council meeting. The crisis-engulfed Fifa president received a fresh demand for “information or documents” in writing from Uefa, which detailed a lengthy list of issues which he failed to satisfy them on last week. “Any refusal to disclose information or documents should be justified individually, with a clear explanation of the specific grounds relied upon,” says an accompanying letter from Theodore Theodoridis, Uefa’s secretary general.

news.title: Uefa gives Infantino two-week deadline to release key documents
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been president of Fifa since 2016 and is standing for re-election for a third time. European governing body Uefa has told Fifa it must release key documents relating to its governance and decision-making by a deadline of 2 November. At the Fifa Council on Thursday, president Gianni Infantino apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan - but failed to release documents relating to the proposal. In a letter seen by BBC Sport, Uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis said that world football's governing body had failed to address "a number of fundamental questions".

news.title: ‘Messi’s plant’: Scientists name newly discovered endangered Andean species after Argentina’s World Cup-w
news.lede: Lionel Messi has spent much of his career collecting football’s biggest honours, but his name has now been attached to something rather different: a newly identified plant growing high in the Peruvian Andes. Named Salvia messii, the species has pale blue and white flowers resembling Argentina’s national colours, a fitting tribute to the player who represented his country 208 times. The botanical honour also comes with a warning, because researchers have classified the plant as endangered.A plant named after one of Argentina’s greatest footballersThe newly described species, Salvia messii, is endemic to the Andes of central and southern Peru, where it grows on rocky, arid slopes at elevations of between 2,000 and 2,400 metres.

news.title: England women's coach Wiegman extends contract to 2029
news.lede: Oct 19 - England coach Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract until the end of the 2029 Women's European Championship, the Football Association announced on Monday. • Wiegman, who took charge in September 2021, led the team to their first major trophy at the 2022 Euros, which they retained three years later. • Under the Dutchwoman, England also reached the Women's World Cup final in Australia and New Zealand in 2023, where they finished runners-up to Spain. • "I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football," Wiegman said in a statement.
